result.title: HandWorldBench: A Unified Benchmark for Hand-Centric World Models
result.summary: Recent advances in world models are opening new possibilities for fine-grained embodied tasks, with hand-object interaction offering a particularly demanding setting. Modeling these interactions involves capturing how hand actions change objects and how the resulting states persist over time. Yet systematic evaluation tailored to these hand-centric capabilities remains underdeveloped. To address this gap, we introduce HandWorldBench, a unified benchmark that systematically evaluates hand-centric world models across human hands, simulated dexterous hands, and real dexterous hands along six dimensions: visual quality, hand fidelity, appearance consistency, instruction following, physical consistency, and temporal coherence. To construct the benchmark, we develop a data curation pipeline that extracts hand-object interaction clips and screens them for quality, yielding 20,500 high-quality egocentric clips from over 600 hours of footage. We then manually select 500 clips covering seven task families for evaluation. Benchmarking eleven models under a unified protocol reveals that stronger hand-pose control does not consistently translate into coherent object-state evolution and persistence or robust cross-embodiment performance, with several specialized hand-control models underperforming general-purpose text/image-to-video generators on dexterous-hand tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出以手部为中心的世界模型统一基准 HandWorldBench：从 600 余小时第一视角视频中筛选出 20,500 段高质量手物交互片段，再人工挑选 500 段覆盖七类任务，按视觉质量、手部保真、外观一致性、指令遵循、物理一致性和时间连贯性六个维度统一评测 11 个模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「物理一致性／物体状态演变与持续」评测维度可能为核查 latent 视觉状态是否保留任务必要细节与状态延续提供外部参照，但该基准面向视频生成质量而非 VLM 内部推理状态，迁移价值需核查。
